doc.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Working full time and standing in for Bob Barnard
summary: He works full time, gets many calls because he plays many instruments, and fills in when Bob Barnard is away.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So do you work now, I hope this isn’t an obvious question, do you work full time as a musician, as a performer?
And is there enough gigs in Australia that you can pretty much do all right?

Yeah, there’s lots. I could work more than I am. Because playing all the instruments, I get calls from more bands than like guys that just play one horn. Plus I lead two bands of my own and I’m in a big band. And it’s a good thing Bob Barnard, because Bob is the king in Australia, you know, he’s the man, he’s out of the country a lot, which is good for me. So when they can’t get Bob they ring me. And so I’m there a lot of the time. And we all do festivals in Melbourne and Adelaide, and interstate things, for pretty good money. So there’s a lot going.
